_anonymised_copy: Anonymised copy of a registered protocol file: internal provenance fields (storage ids, hosts, resource accounting, internal review notes) were removed or redacted. Embedded sha256 values refer to the original registered file and do not match this copy.
supersedes: the audit part of A1 (single-annotator audit of sheet rows 1-100, tipping-point labels AUDIT_ROBUST / AUDIT_SENSITIVE, audited-subset estimate) and the rule's blinding clause 'no Hits on R2 until the sheet returns'. A1's PRIMARY set (all judge-accepted rewrites) is kept.
reason: On R1, adversarially removing 23-35 of 569 rewrites (4.0-6.2%) breaks the Holm test of drop(G_k) - drop(P_k) > 0, and invalid rewrites plausibly favour the parser (it snaps to the original template). The rewrites that drive the contrast must therefore be reviewed, not only a random sample. Mirrors the R1 audit protocol v2.
status_at_amendment: as in A1: sample and pool drawn, prompts written, weights downloading; no R2 rewrite, judge call, prediction or score exists

design.PRIMARY: unchanged from A1: H1-H3 (drop(G_k) - drop(P_k) > 0, k = 1, 5, 100) on all judge-accepted R2 rewrites; paired Poisson(1) bootstrap B = 10,000, seed 20261029; one-sided p = share of bootstrap means <= 0; Holm over the three; CONFIRMED iff Holm-adjusted p < 0.05, else NOT_CONFIRMED; LOW_N if n < 200. Secondary descriptive analyses unchanged.
design.blinding_and_order: 1) generate, check and judge the rewrites and freeze the perturbed set; 2) run all frozen arms; 3) save the sha256 freeze of every R2 prediction file as an artifact; 4) only then score: the PRIMARY H1-H3 (final; no longer wait for the audit), the secondaries, and the per-question contrasts c_k(q) = drop(G_k)(q) - drop(P_k)(q), with S and P hits averaged over their 3 S-seed files and G at seed 0, as in R1; 5) build the audit kit from c_k. The annotator never sees predictions, hits, c_k, the judge output or the selection flags.
design.audit_selection: T = every judge-accepted rewrite with c_k(q) > 0 at any k in {1, 5, 100}. R = a simple random sample of 100 judge-accepted rewrites: sorted(quids)[i] for i in numpy.random.default_rng([20261029, 7]).choice(n, size = min(100, n), replace = False). Audit set = T union R. Presentation: numpy.random.default_rng([20261029, 8]).permutation over the audit set in ascending quid order; audit ids A001, A002, ... in that order; no column shows targeted vs random. Analyst-only selection key (audit_id, quid, in_random100, in_targeted, favourP_k1, favourP_k5, favourP_k100) in key_do_not_open_before_review/.
design.annotator: single annotator (one author), blind to model outputs, hits, the judge output, the key and the selection flags; reviews every audit row
design.accept_rule: same_answer_set == Y and same_constraint_time == Y; N, unsure or blank = not accepted

audit_analyses.random100: acceptance rate of R with Wilson 95% CI (z = 1.959964), and the rejection rate with its Wilson CI
audit_analyses.targeted: acceptance rate of T with Wilson 95% CI
audit_analyses.BOUND: H1-H3 recomputed on the judge-accepted rewrites minus the human-rejected rows (same bootstrap B = 10,000, seed 20261029, one-sided, Holm over k); BOUND_HOLDS iff the Holm-adjusted p < 0.05, else BOUND_FAILS. The scorer asserts that every unreviewed row has c_k <= 0 at every k, so the unreviewed rows cannot create a positive contrast.
audit_analyses.descriptive: contrasts on the audited-and-accepted rows only; per-arm drops after removing the rejected rows; the pre-review adversarial tipping point per k (A1 algorithm, no label)

design.paper_wording: 'human-audited by one author: all rewrites on which the parser outperformed the reader plus a random 100'
design.kit: drafts/manuscripts/pakdd2027/dossier_2026-10-28/review_kit_R2/ with AUDIT_R2_INSTRUCTIONS.md (modelled on review_kit/AUDIT_R1_INSTRUCTIONS.md), the audit sheet (.xlsx and .csv), and analyst-only files (selection key, gold, scorer, protocol) in key_do_not_open_before_review/
